instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, changing the water until it runs clear, then drain it. Put the rice in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave the lid on until the curry is ready.

Cut the chicken into 1 1/2-inch pieces and pat them dry. Transfer them to a bowl and add 1 tsp of the grated ginger, 1 minced garlic clove, the turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt. Toss and leave it while you chop.
Finely chop the onion and the tomato. Mince the remaining 2 garlic cloves and grate the remaining 1 tsp ginger. Crush the peppercorns coarsely with a mortar and pestle or under the bottom of a pan.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the cumin, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom. After about 20 seconds they will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the curry leaves and stand back a little. They will spatter. Stir for 10 seconds.
Add the onion and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring often, until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute, until the raw smell is gone.
Add the tomato and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 4 minutes, until it is soft and the moisture has mostly cooked off.
Stir in the paprika, garam masala and crushed pepper. Cook for 30 seconds.
Turn the heat to medium-high and add the chicken in a single layer. Cook for 4 minutes, turning, until the outside is no longer pink.
Turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 8 minutes. The chicken gives off enough liquid, so you don't need to add water.

Uncover and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the liquid is gone and the masala coats the chicken. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the thickest piece, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink and the juices run clear.
Take the skillet off the heat and squeeze in the juice of half the lemon. Cut the other half into wedges.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes (Pepper Chicken, 4.98 from 186) is the lead, taken in its dry style: whole spices in oil, curry leaves, onion, ginger, garlic and tomato cooked down, crushed pepper, then the chicken cooked covered and finished uncovered until the masala clings, with lemon at the end. The other two pages read (Pavani's Kitchen 5 from 1 vote, Palate's Desire 4.89 from 9) add a fennel and cumin pepper blend and a curry leaf tempering but have too few ratings to lead. The lead is named Pepper Chicken rather than Pepper Chicken Fry, and it is the same dish in its dry form. Boneless thighs replace bone-in pieces so it cooks in about 30 minutes, and the heat comes only from pepper; no green chilies. It is a dry dish by design, so there is no sauce.
